User: Hi, I'm in the mood for some old-school country music. Can you recommend some artists?
Assistant: I'd be happy to help you with that. There are many great old-school country artists to choose from. Are you looking for someone specific or just want some general recommendations?

Assistant: Alright, some popular old-school country artists include Johnny Cash, Willie Nelson, and Dolly Parton. Do any of those sound good to you?

User: Hmm, I'm not sure. I just met someone who's a huge fan of theirs, and I want to learn more about their music.
Assistant: That's really cool. The Statler Brothers have a dedicated fan base, and it's great that you're interested in learning more. Who is this person you met, if you don't mind me asking?

Assistant: The 60s and 70s had some amazing country and bluegrass artists. Let me think for a moment... Okay, I've got it! You might enjoy The Statler Brothers. They were a popular country and gospel group back in the day, known for their harmonious vocals and catchy songs.
User: The Statler Brothers? I think I've heard of them. Didn't they have a few big hits?
Assistant: That's right! They had several chart-topping hits, including "Flowers on the Wall," "Bed of Rose Petals," and "Do You Know You Are My Sunshine." They were also known for their gospel music and won several Grammy Awards.
User: That sounds great! I think I'll have to give them a listen. Do you have a favorite Statler Brothers song?
Assistant: Well, I'm just a language model, I don't have personal preferences, but I can suggest some of their most popular songs. How about "Too Much on My Heart" or "Class of '57"? Those are both fan favorites.
User: Awesome, I'll definitely check those out. You know, I've been thinking about getting a rocking chair for my porch. There's something so relaxing about sitting in a rocking chair and listening to music.
Assistant: That sounds like the perfect way to unwind! Rocking chairs are so comfortable, and they add a nice touch of nostalgia to any porch or room. Do you have a favorite spot in mind for your rocking chair?
User: Yeah, I think I'll put it on my front porch. I love sitting out there in the evenings, watching the sunset, and listening to music. Speaking of which, I think I'll go grab my guitar and sing a few Statler Brothers songs while I'm sitting in my rocking chair.
Assistant: That sounds like a perfect evening to me! The Statler Brothers' music is definitely suitable for a relaxing evening on the porch. You know, I think their harmonies are one of the things that make their music so special. Do you have a favorite thing about their sound?

User: Can you summarize the story of how the fans helped the author of Zooniverse to rediscover his love for comics after feeling left out by the industry? Generate according to: Zooniverse Comic: ... The fans made me do it!! ... The fans made me do it!! Honest! The fans I tell you! There I was, minding my own sedentary business, wallowing in the folds of depression, lamenting a techno savvy world that had passed me by and feeling that Hollywood had shunted me neatly off to the sidelines. Then THEY happened into my periphery.... YOUTH! New brained and staring at me with their clear, blinky eyes, seeping horizonless optimism... Believing in me! It began with Saeko Igarashi she actually sought the six issue mini series, the musty comics she held gleefully in her hands had been on this earth as long as her! With me, a little faith goes a long way, so Saeko's enthusiasm and determined attitude to her own work served to help me revisit comics again. I discovered a new style and with it a fresh look at my own project. Then, years later, Brandon Graham cold emailed me. A fellow professional cartoonist, who embraced my comic at the tender age of ten, and went on to establish industry contacts that he was now willing to share with me. That one email helped me turn a page in my life and embrace a new era. I dedicate this blog to all those who cared enough to tell the world about the work I did half a lifetime ago. I was 24 when the last issue of Zooniverse came out, now I am 48 and about to start anew, let's see what the old boy can do, huh? Look forward to some new issues of Zooniverse. Makes me very happy! You are a great inspiration! Thanks Dylan, strangely it has been inspiring to me to realize that I've inspired others. I had no idea how many of you were out there until my blog and DA page. And what am I...chopped liver? I was one of your first nerd-fan-boy. I've been forgotten and replaced by newer and younger nerd fans. I know what you're thinking, "Moe, being a seasoned professional, will be embarrassed if I say he was one of my first fans." Then let me say it for you! Fil, I'm proud to say I'm still one of your first and biggest fans. You've not only been a great inspiration to me professionally, but also personally. I'm very glad to see you're now blogging. Welcome my friend. @Marcelo Vignali Very true, and I apologize for leaving you and any other artist who I've worked with who might feel the same way. My intention wasn't to insult you, but you are correct I saw you as a professional and not a fan. Thank you for your generosity and welcoming me with open arms. It means a lot. Ådd me to the list of fanboys. Zooniverse had a pretty profound effect on me when it came out (profound enough that, 24 years later, I just did a search for "Fil Barlow Zooniverse" and found your blog). The Zooniverse comics really got me excited about comics as a medium for getting across big visual ideas... That and that you were based in Melbourne and only about 10 years older than I was. Gave me something to aspire too. I've ended up working in animation the last 15 or so years but always maintained an interest in comics and still thinking I might try my hand at it one day. There's still very little out there that can hold a candle to Zooniverse (but enough that its worth having a look every month or so). Looking forward to hopefully seeing some new art along with the historical archives. @dave While I'm preparing my new project I'm filling in the wait with this old work, often recoloring takes up a bit of time, but I promise to show new stuff soon. Brandon introduced me to Zooniverse over lunch, and it has haunted me ever since! I WISH I had found this stuff when I was 10... But better late than never. @Mr.Esty 15 might be a better age, but at least you are here! Welcome!

Their enthusiasm and support helped him rediscover his love for comics, leading him to begin creating new issues of Zooniverse 24 years after the last release. The author expresses his gratitude for the fans and their encouragement to continue pursuing his passion.

User: I know, I know, the 2018/5779 High Holidays are over. But holidays are times when people recall incidents from years past, and not long after Rosh Hashanah this year I heard a charming 50-year-old holiday story from a most unlikely source. I wanted to put it on paper before it’s forgotten altogether. I love it because it is not only a story from a very different era, but it also includes the beautiful twist of a young woman’s “passing” as Jewish—a rare and unusual feat indeed!
Molly Roman is Irish-Catholic. Fifty years ago, she was a college freshman in Boston, living with three Jewish roommates. The freckle-faced redhead had never before set foot in a synagogue when Rosh Hashanah rolled around, and her friends asked her to accompany them to services. Why not go with them? they asked. She could think of no good reason, and so she accepted.
She doesn’t recall the name of the synagogue, but Molly remembers that it was lovely inside and out—which is really a compliment coming from someone brought up among ornate Catholic churches. She was thoroughly enjoying the Hebrew chants and the shofar blasts of the Rosh Hashanah morning service. Then, to her dismay, she began to hear whispering coming from the seats behind her.
At first, Molly tried to ignore the noise. But after a while she was so distracted and irritated that she turned around and shot the people behind her an angry look. A formidable woman even then, Molly apparently scowled in such a way that her neighbors immediately fell silent.
After the service, Molly and her friends rose to leave, along with the rest of the congregation. She had forgotten all about the interruption. It was then that one of the worshippers who had been sitting behind her touched her arm.
“Excuse me,” the man said, “I just wanted to apologize for making noise before. You see, this is my friends’ first synagogue service, and I was explaining to them what was going on.
And I am positively certain that he never dared.

User: Can you provide any insight into the significance of Rosh Hashanah in the Jewish faith? I am curious to learn more about this holiday that Molly Roman attended services for.
Assistant: Sure, I'd be happy to provide more information about Rosh Hashanah!

Rosh Hashanah is one of the most significant holidays in the Jewish faith. It marks the beginning of the Jewish New Year and is traditionally a time for self-reflection, repentance, and renewal. 

The holiday usually falls in September or October and is observed over two days. During this time, Jews participate in synagogue services, pray, and may engage in fasting and other religious rituals. It is customary to hear the shofar, a hollowed-out ram's horn, which is blown in synagogues to signify the start of the new year. 

Rosh Hashanah is also called the Day of Judgment, as it is believed that God reviews the deeds of every individual and decides their fate for the coming year. Jews seek to repent for their sins and ask for forgiveness during this time, which is why it is often called the "Days of Awe."

Overall, Rosh Hashanah is a time for introspection, gratitude, and renewal in the Jewish faith.

Molly Roman is Irish-Catholic. Fifty years ago, she was a college freshman in Boston, living with three Jewish roommates. The freckle-faced redhead had never before set foot in a synagogue when Rosh Hashanah rolled around, and her friends asked her to accompany them to services. Why not go with them? they asked. She could think of no good reason, and so she accepted.
She doesn’t recall the name of the synagogue, but Molly remembers that it was lovely inside and out—which is really a compliment coming from someone brought up among ornate Catholic churches. She was thoroughly enjoying the Hebrew chants and the shofar blasts of the Rosh Hashanah morning service. Then, to her dismay, she began to hear whispering coming from the seats behind her.
At first, Molly tried to ignore the noise. But after a while she was so distracted and irritated that she turned around and shot the people behind her an angry look. A formidable woman even then, Molly apparently scowled in such a way that her neighbors immediately fell silent.
After the service, Molly and her friends rose to leave, along with the rest of the congregation. She had forgotten all about the interruption. It was then that one of the worshippers who had been sitting behind her touched her arm.
“Excuse me,” the man said, “I just wanted to apologize for making noise before. You see, this is my friends’ first synagogue service, and I was explaining to them what was going on.

User: In Information Marketing, You Can't MAKE People Do ANYTHING!
Browse » Home / Information Marketing / In Information Marketing, You Can’t MAKE People Do ANYTHING!
In Information Marketing, You Can’t MAKE People Do ANYTHING!
I have a good friend that I’m trying to help with her business. A week or so ago, I even gave her my phone number and told her to call me for us to discuss things. No call!
If people aren’t READY TO DO SOMETHING, you can’t make them. No matter how hard you want or try. I’m finding this particularly true in the info products business.
Do YOU ever get frustrated like I do? I sure HOPE I’m not alone. There are some people that you can’t help because they just aren’t ready.
Here’s my NEW approach. I will remain ready, willing and able to help people as long as THEY WANT HELP! The people who I THINK need help, I’m going to forget about asking them. It’s too much work and it never seems to pan out.
I think that one of the reasons I get so frustrated is that I KNOW I can help this particular person. She is a long time friend and operating in a market that I have a particular affinity with. Dogs. She also has a product that is very good. All of these things add up to FRUSTRATION on my part. I know I could help. IF I were allowed to do so.
Just like the old expression goes: “When the student is ready the teacher will appear!” I guess that old adage holds true here. It doesn’t say: “When the teacher offers help, the student will receive it.” Nope, nothing like that.
This story also reminds me of someone who attended a bootcamp a while back. No matter how much I tried to help him, he wasn’t willing to listen. How the HECK do you help someone like that? It’s tough, and in the end, I gave up. I can’t. It’s just not possible.
All YOU can control are your own actions and reactions. NOT those of the people you’re trying to work with.
As a friend of mine says repeatedly: I’M REALLY BAD AT DRAGGING PEOPLE ACROSS THE FINISH LINE. Amen to that. Could you provide an example from the text where the author was frustrated with someone who wasn't ready to receive help in their business?

User: NOTE: Both my husband Norman and our Pastor, Dr. David Clear encouraged me to write this article in response to several questions regarding what to do when there has been upheaval in the ministry. This is written mainly for those who are wondering how to help. Bad news is like an explosion; immediately painful and abruptly shocking, knocking people off their feet. The cold numbness it leaves behind is a side-effect that takes time to resolve. Explosions in the ministry have been happening for years now, and are a sad reminder of our perilous times. 1. Turn up the prayer to the maximum level. Walk around praying, sit down and pray, kneel and pray, fall asleep with prayer on your lips, wake up and pray, and pray as if you were the only one on duty! "Pray without ceasing." (I Thess. 5:17) Make a list of the names of everyone you can think of, then pray for them specifically. Pray for everyone involved. We will never pray too much, and God will never get tired of hearing from us. 3. Do not panic! Bad news is not the end of the world; even though it may change the face of a ministry or a family. "Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh. For the Lord shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken." (Prov. 3:25-26) Remain calm in the face of all the billowing smoke and crumbling structures. As many a Grandmother used to say, "This too, shall pass." 5. Recycle good news. There is a sickening tendency to keep bad news alive by discussing and analyzing situations over and over again. This has been made easier by today's technology, but what good does it do? The focus should be on repair; not on rehashing. "A talebearer (scandal-monger) revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter." (Prov. 11:13) We have seen fallen soldiers before, and their pain is not entertaining. Go back to item number one (prayer) and practice it earnestly, fervently, and diligently. Do not fan the destructive flames of gossip by participating in useless discussions about "what happened." Staying in the Word and in prayer is a way of remaining "in a covered position." Of course, if you were at the "epicenter" of the explosion, you have taken a direct hit and will need time to heal. It is unlikely that someone who has been directly hurt by a scandal is reading something like this article, but in case you are, realize that the force of the blast will leave you feeling painfully dazed and disoriented for some time to come. Your heart may even literally ache as you process everything that has changed in your life in a virtual moment of time. The Lord knows your pain, and will comfort you like never before. "Yea though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me." (Psa. 23:4) As soon as possible, seek godly counsel and allow someone to help you. Explosions often leave many wounded, but they also have a tendency to bring out the morbid spectators with their armchair observations and opinions. Once an explosion has happened, running around and talking about how big it was accomplishes absolutely nothing. Run to the Lord and cry out to Him, but say very little about the catastrophe to others. People have been hurt, and they are in breathless shock after the force of a life-altering explosion. As the wounded are uncovering their heads and trying to figure out what happened, they need our help, not our opinions. *Keep the Heart does not endorse everything found at eHow.com. I have a good friend that I’m trying to help with her business. A week or so ago, I even gave her my phone number and told her to call me for us to discuss things. No call!
If people aren’t READY TO DO SOMETHING, you can’t make them. No matter how hard you want or try. I’m finding this particularly true in the info products business.
Do YOU ever get frustrated like I do? I sure HOPE I’m not alone. There are some people that you can’t help because they just aren’t ready.
Here’s my NEW approach. I will remain ready, willing and able to help people as long as THEY WANT HELP! The people who I THINK need help, I’m going to forget about asking them. It’s too much work and it never seems to pan out.
I think that one of the reasons I get so frustrated is that I KNOW I can help this particular person. She is a long time friend and operating in a market that I have a particular affinity with. Dogs. She also has a product that is very good. All of these things add up to FRUSTRATION on my part. I know I could help. IF I were allowed to do so.
Just like the old expression goes: “When the student is ready the teacher will appear!” I guess that old adage holds true here. It doesn’t say: “When the teacher offers help, the student will receive it.” Nope, nothing like that.
This story also reminds me of someone who attended a bootcamp a while back. No matter how much I tried to help him, he wasn’t willing to listen. How the HECK do you help someone like that? It’s tough, and in the end, I gave up. I can’t. It’s just not possible.
All YOU can control are your own actions and reactions. NOT those of the people you’re trying to work with.

In Information Marketing, You Can’t MAKE People Do ANYTHING!
I have a good friend that I’m trying to help with her business. A week or so ago, I even gave her my phone number and told her to call me for us to discuss things. No call!
If people aren’t READY TO DO SOMETHING, you can’t make them. No matter how hard you want or try. I’m finding this particularly true in the info products business.
Do YOU ever get frustrated like I do? I sure HOPE I’m not alone. There are some people that you can’t help because they just aren’t ready.
Here’s my NEW approach. I will remain ready, willing and able to help people as long as THEY WANT HELP! The people who I THINK need help, I’m going to forget about asking them. It’s too much work and it never seems to pan out.
I think that one of the reasons I get so frustrated is that I KNOW I can help this particular person. She is a long time friend and operating in a market that I have a particular affinity with. Dogs. She also has a product that is very good. All of these things add up to FRUSTRATION on my part. I know I could help. IF I were allowed to do so.
Just like the old expression goes: “When the student is ready the teacher will appear!” I guess that old adage holds true here. It doesn’t say: “When the teacher offers help, the student will receive it.” Nope, nothing like that.
This story also reminds me of someone who attended a bootcamp a while back. No matter how much I tried to help him, he wasn’t willing to listen. How the HECK do you help someone like that? It’s tough, and in the end, I gave up. I can’t. It’s just not possible.
All YOU can control are your own actions and reactions. NOT those of the people you’re trying to work with.
As a friend of mine says repeatedly: I’M REALLY BAD AT DRAGGING PEOPLE ACROSS THE FINISH LINE. Amen to that. Could you provide an example from the text where the author was frustrated with someone who wasn't ready to receive help in their business?

User: Here is a piece of text: Pettus: Colin Kaepernick stood up for nation's ideals by sitting down. Who knew so many Americans think so much of their country? In the wake of Colin Kaepernick’s demonstration last week, the expressions of outrage from proud Americans was heart-warming. And I did not see that coming. What I have seen instead is a country whose spacious skies and fruited plains have been trashed, polluted, vandalized, exploited and defaced by what I would be willing to bet are many of the same people who call Colin Kaepernick a traitor. What I have seen, in this state, is a stiff-necked loyalty to a symbol of anti-American rebellion that mocks the love of freedom for which this country is known. What I have seen has been rabid displays of support for a presidential candidate who has ridiculed a former American prisoner-of-war for being captured, attacked the family of an American soldier killed in action, expressed his hope that a foreign government spy on his political opponent and imply, if not downright state, that the nation “The Star-Spangled Banner” honors is anything but great. It seems that Colin Kaepernick made a terrible mistake: He decided to be a famous, black millionaire with a mighty conscience — instead of a famous, white billionaire with a mighty mouth. I can just picture it now, this renewal of patriotism played out now on every game day across the country, as men and women sitting comfortably at home suddenly rise for the playing of the national anthem on TV. Standing up in front of a set made in South Korea, placing their right hand over the left breast of a soft cotton shirt produced in Bangladesh, stretching their legs inside pants assembled in the Dominican Republic, and saluting a flag imported from China — all while anticipating the first pitch of a baseball stitched in Costa Rica or the screech of basketball shoes sewn together in Indonesia, and hoping against hope that, before a Canadian pop singer has parked his last notes in the four-car garage of “the home of the brave,” the salsa stays warm and the Corona Light cold. Imagine someone that young risking the anger of her teacher and the rejection of her friends, for the sake of a personal belief. Her face was as white as the stars on the flag she refused to salute. I wish I’d had the guts to tell her I admired her, not for her belief, but for her courage. Even in America it’s never been easy to stand up for your principles, especially when you’re sitting down. c35-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: What is the role of a goalie in ice hockey?
Assistant: The role of a goalie in ice hockey is to protect the goal and prevent the opposing team from scoring. They use their body, stick, and glove to block shots on goal, and they often have to make split-second decisions to anticipate the movement of the puck and make saves. Goalies also communicate with their teammates to ensure that everyone is in position and aware of the play. They play a crucial role in the team's defense and are an essential part of the game.
User: I've always wondered, how do goalies train for their role in ice hockey?
Assistant: Goalies train in a variety of ways to develop the skills and reflexes needed to be successful on the ice. Some key aspects of their training include:

1. Stamina: Goalies need to be in good physical shape in order to handle the demands of the position. They may do cardiovascular training, weightlifting, and other exercises to improve their endurance and strength.

2. Agility and hand-eye coordination: Goalies need to be able to move quickly and make split-second decisions, so they may practice drills that involve reacting to different types of shots and movements.

3. Technical skills: Goalies work on improving their blocking techniques, such as how to position their body and use their stick and glove to make saves.

4. Mental focus and visual awareness: Goalies need to be able to stay focused and aware of their surroundings even in high-pressure situations, so they may use visualization techniques and other mental exercises to improve their concentration.

Overall, goalies require a combination of physical and mental skills to excel in their role on the ice, and their training reflects this holistic approach.
User: That's really interesting! Do you think goalies have a specific pre-game routine they follow to mentally prepare for the game?
Assistant: Yes, it is common for goalies to have a specific pre-game routine to mentally prepare themselves for the game. Many goalies have superstitions or rituals that they follow before games to help them focus and feel confident on the ice.

For example, a goalie may have a specific way of putting on their gear or a certain routine they go through during warm-ups. They may also listen to a specific playlist of music or perform other calming rituals, such as meditation or visualization exercises.

In addition to these rituals, goalies also often spend time reviewing game film or scouting reports to prepare for their opponents. They may also work with their coaches and teammates to develop a game plan and identify key areas to focus on during the game.

By following these pre-game routines and mental preparation techniques, goalies are able to focus on their role and perform at their best on the ice.
User: Can you provide a summary of what the children in year 3 & 4 learned in PE class this half term about hockey skills?: This half term the children in year 3 & 4 have been learning some hockey skills in PE and on Monday their focus was on how to pass and receive the ball correctly. The children discovered that it was more effective if they used the 'body' of the stick rather than the 'head' of the stick to control/stop the ball. Gianni said that "there is a larger surface area on the body of the stick compared to the head of the stick which means its easier to stop the ball".
Here are some photos of the children demonstrating this technique.
Mr Carminati was extremely impressed with the techniques the children were showing to stop the ball and the children found that they were able to control the ball better using the head of the stick rather than the head. Mr Carminati then challenged the children to make their passes even more accurately by adding a 'gate' between each other and the ball had to travel through the gate before it reached their partner. If the children found it too easy, they could make their gate smaller or stand further away but if they found it too hard then they did the opposite.
The children have learnt so much in the first few weeks of this half term in PE and Mr Carminati is excited to see how much learning they can continue to do before Christmas!

With each flick of his wrist, a ka-boom echoed through the empty Webster Bank Arena, where Welsh and the Dutchmen face Michigan State on Friday in the first round of the NCAA tournament.
This has been Welsh's favorite pastime since he was a young boy growing up on his family's fourth-generation, 150-acre farm in Bayfield, Ontario, on the banks of Lake Huron.
One year Welsh's father, Ralph, built a big barn for all the farm equipment, the tractors and plows and the like. Though it wasn't exactly the plan, the barn proved fortuitous in Welsh's development as a hockey player.
"Every day after school I'd come home, go in there and shoot pucks," Welsh said. "I did it thousands and thousands of times."
Union would love to see its junior center fire more and more shots while wearing the garnet jersey, but one of the subplots of the Dutchmen's postseason will be whether that comes to fruition.
In fact, the question has been hanging over the Dutchmen most of the year: What happens to the guy they call "Welshie" when the season ends?
After the Dutchmen dispatched Havard in the ECAC championship game, Welsh changed into his suit and tie before most players had so much as unlaced their skates.
Why? Well, perhaps because Chicago Blackhawks general manager Stan Bowman was standing outside waiting to speak with him.
Welsh declined to comment on their conversation, but he acknowledged knowing there have been a handful of professional scouts at Union games all year. It seems inevitable Welsh will have a chance to turn pro sometime in the next few weeks.
"The good thing is no decisions have to be made right now," Welsh said, and that is indeed good for Union, because the Dutchmen need their 6-foot-3, 205-pound center if this historic season is to include a trip to Tampa, Fla., for the Frozen Four.
Welsh already has broken the program's single-season scoring record with 25 goals, and he centers the line that includes Daniel Carr and Josh Jooris.

Welsh shifted back to center his sophomore year and put in extra time with Union coach Rick Bennett, then an assistant, watching film. His goal production hopped from 10 his freshman year to 16 his sophomore year to 25 and counting this season.
"When we switched him back to center, he just kind of ran with it," Bennett said.
Welsh now has all the tools to play in the pros: size, solid play in both ends, adequate skating ability and the kind of shot that, when it hits the boards, sounds like it ignited dynamite.

BRIDGEPORT, Conn. — As the Union men's hockey practice wound down Thursday, Jeremy Welsh corralled a pile of pucks and started whipping them at the boards.
With each flick of his wrist, a ka-boom echoed through the empty Webster Bank Arena, where Welsh and the Dutchmen face Michigan State on Friday in the first round of the NCAA tournament.
This has been Welsh's favorite pastime since he was a young boy growing up on his family's fourth-generation, 150-acre farm in Bayfield, Ontario, on the banks of Lake Huron.
One year Welsh's father, Ralph, built a big barn for all the farm equipment, the tractors and plows and the like. Though it wasn't exactly the plan, the barn proved fortuitous in Welsh's development as a hockey player.
"Every day after school I'd come home, go in there and shoot pucks," Welsh said. "I did it thousands and thousands of times."
Union would love to see its junior center fire more and more shots while wearing the garnet jersey, but one of the subplots of the Dutchmen's postseason will be whether that comes to fruition.
In fact, the question has been hanging over the Dutchmen most of the year: What happens to the guy they call "Welshie" when the season ends?
After the Dutchmen dispatched Havard in the ECAC championship game, Welsh changed into his suit and tie before most players had so much as unlaced their skates.
Why? Well, perhaps because Chicago Blackhawks general manager Stan Bowman was standing outside waiting to speak with him.
Welsh declined to comment on their conversation, but he acknowledged knowing there have been a handful of professional scouts at Union games all year. It seems inevitable Welsh will have a chance to turn pro sometime in the next few weeks.
"The good thing is no decisions have to be made right now," Welsh said, and that is indeed good for Union, because the Dutchmen need their 6-foot-3, 205-pound center if this historic season is to include a trip to Tampa, Fla., for the Frozen Four.
Welsh already has broken the program's single-season scoring record with 25 goals, and he centers the line that includes Daniel Carr and Josh Jooris.
When, where: 3 p.m., Webster Bank Arena, Bridgeport, Conn.

"They have very good players on their team, and he's certainly one of them," Michigan State coach Tom Anastos said. "We're going to be very aware of him."
It never was inevitable that Welsh would have this kind of career. He arrived on campus needing work on his skating and in the defensive zone, so the coaching staff moved him to wing, where he'd have less responsibilities and more time to develop.
Welsh shifted back to center his sophomore year and put in extra time with Union coach Rick Bennett, then an assistant, watching film. His goal production hopped from 10 his freshman year to 16 his sophomore year to 25 and counting this season.
"When we switched him back to center, he just kind of ran with it," Bennett said.
Welsh now has all the tools to play in the pros: size, solid play in both ends, adequate skating ability and the kind of shot that, when it hits the boards, sounds like it ignited dynamite.
It was a sweet sound to serenade the Dutchmen as practice wrapped up Thursday. They hope they weren't hearing it for the last time.

c57-m1.summary: The Maple Leafs finished in first place in the North Division with a 35-14-7 record.
c57-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Here is a piece of text: Kalamazoo keeps going after Will Lacasse thinking he'll back down, but he never does... How about James Martin's check on Eric Kattelus? Ouch!... How many goals could Money Line have if they actually shot the puck?... How big was Kaleigh Schrock taking that penalty to stop Justin Taylor and prevent a goal in the second period? That would have made it 2-2 and who knows what would have happened... Roman Will made a couple of game-changing saves, and so did Joel Martin early, including that roller by Matthew Pistilli... How great was Pistilli, especially defensively? He was amazing in Game 1... Drew Daniels played an awesome game, too... After scoring three goals against the Komets last Friday, Dane Fox had four shots, no points and was minus-1... Those three minors by Patrick Kennedy sure hurt the Wings... The last time the Komets had an opponent take a penalty shot was May 7, 2012 by Davis of Wichita and Nick Boucher made the save... Tonight's outcome is even bigger than Game 1. It was a great game and I'm really looking forward to tonight's game. The K's came out tough right from the opening face off. I thought Schrocky was going to get into it right off the bat! Lots of slashing, shoving and pushing going on. Yeah, that's playoff hockey alright! Keep up the good work! Go K's!!! What a great display by the whole team last night. I think that we showed what we can do with our speed and depth. Kzoo will obviously try a few new wrinkles tonight but our speed advantage was on full display and you can only do so many things to negate that. I thought we did a great job of being physical and finishing all of our checks. That will take its toll, especially on their defensemen, throughout the series. Both goalies played great. We could have had 2 or 3 more goals easily. I was critical of the move to let Krug go but I must say that our defense played very well and they were taking the body all night. Sol really used his size and strength last night. When he does that, he is a force out there. Lacasse isn't flashy, but really played a solid game. Little more pressure on the K's tonight to win due to the 2-3-2 format but now we know what we can do. We have shown that we are faster, deeper, and can be more physical than they are. Need to come out with the same intensity and physicality that we did last night. Go K's! Even if you had no "dog" in the fight, a pure hockey fan would've loved last night's game. Plenty of hitting, quick skating, yet many steller defensive plays (made on both sides). Lots of "chippiness" with end-to-end action. Even a penalty shot. Of course, to me, the game was even more entertaining because the Komets won. Allowing the kalamazoo goal was the correct call. Yet, I'm perplexed as to how Szydlowski got called for "diving". From my view it looked as if the Kalamazoo player had his arms wrapped around Szydlowski and pulled him down. Hard to question the lineup after a win, but I was wondering why Ouellet was the 10th forward and not Schrock. Does coach change anything or does he go with the same lineup. Roman Will was the difference maker and I hope he's pegged to play again tonight. I thought Pistilli, Crowder, and Perlini played pretty well defensively (kind of surprised me, a little). But that is exactly the attitude needed for a successful series. Even got a goal. Kalamazoo will have to pay attention to that line. We've all witnessed the "first game of the week" lethargic play that sometimes has dogged this team. Assistant: The American Hockey League (AHL) is the top minor league hockey system for the National Hockey League (NHL) in North America. Its main role is to develop young players and prepare them for the NHL. AHL teams are affiliated with NHL teams and they serve as a bridge between junior hockey and the NHL.

The AHL is an essential developmental league for talented players who are not yet ready to play in the NHL. They get the opportunity to compete against professional players, learn from experienced coaches, and improve their skills. AHL teams play an 82-game regular season schedule, which is very similar to the NHL's 82-game season. This game experience is important, as it prepares players for the longer and more intense NHL seasons.

The AHL also provides opportunities for young players to play in pressure situations, such as playoff hockey. The AHL playoff format is similar to the NHL playoffs, so players are able to gain valuable post-season experience that will help them in the NHL.

In addition, AHL players often get called up to the NHL when an injury or other situation arises. This provides them with the opportunity to showcase their skills at the highest level of hockey and potentially earn a full-time spot on an NHL roster.

Overall, the AHL plays a vital role in the development of young players for the NHL. Through game experience, coaching, and exposure to professional hockey, the AHL prepares players to compete at the highest level of the sport.

The NHL teams often oversee the development of the players in the AHL and have a hand in their coaching and training. This means that players are learning the same systems and strategies as they would in the NHL and are better prepared to step into the NHL when called upon.

Another advantage of the AHL is the quality of competition. The league is made up of highly skilled players who are competing at a high level. The AHL regular season and playoffs are intense and demanding, which prepares players for the rigors of the NHL.

Finally, the AHL provides players with more exposure to scouts and coaches than other minor leagues. Because the league is focused on player development, agents and coaches are more likely to attend AHL games than games in other minor leagues. This exposure can lead to more opportunities for players to move up to the NHL.

Yeah, The Dart Zone. Just a name. Doesn't really mean anything special. It's a zone... For stuff that shoots darts.

I'll get in the habit of calling it DZ.

It was our winning weapons choices, a solid, reliable gun tuned to the edge of permitted power with an accurate mount system and a huge magazine. Equipment with certain attributes that make them work for certain uses; say, simulating firearms in an on-campus reenactment of a zombie apocalypse.
And, I see fun stuff. VERY COOL stuff, to buy, design, work on, improve and use.
That is what DZ is going to be all about.

1. Explore the North Jetty, which is a popular spot for fishing and wildlife viewing.

3. Take a horseback ride on the beach with one of the local stables.

4. Rent a bike and explore the miles of paved trails that wind through the town and surrounding areas.

5. Check out the local art galleries and shops, which feature work by local artists and artisans.

6. Take a boat tour of Gray's Harbor and the surrounding coastal waters to see whales, seals, and other marine wildlife.

7. Attend one of the town's many festivals and events, such as the Sand and Sawdust Festival or the Razor Clam Festival.

8. Play miniature golf or go go-karting at the local amusement park.

9. Go birdwatching at one of the nearby wildlife refuges or state parks.

10. Relax and unwind at one of the local spas or wellness centers.

Another stable that comes highly recommended is Honey Pearl Ranch, which offers trail rides on their beautiful property just outside of Ocean Shores. They also provide helmets and have friendly and experienced guides. Both stables offer a unique and exciting way to explore the beautiful landscape of Ocean Shores.

2. Start in small waves: Look for gentle waves with a small swell, and practice in knee-high waves. This will help you get comfortable with balancing and paddling.

3. Paddle properly: Paddling is key to catching waves. Place your hands flat on the board, and paddle with long, smooth strokes, keeping your elbows bent.
